𝗛𝗘 𝗪𝗔𝗦 𝗥𝗜𝗚𝗛𝗧 𝗔𝗕𝗢𝗨𝗧 𝗔𝗜 - 𝗔𝗡𝗗 𝗟𝗢𝗦𝗧 𝟯𝟱 𝗕𝗜𝗟𝗟𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗗𝗢𝗟𝗟𝗔𝗥𝗦 𝗔𝗡𝗬𝗪𝗔𝗬 📉

Last week, one of the most watched funds in the AI trade nearly blew up.

Leopold Aschenbrenner’s fund, Situational Awareness, peaked at around 45 billion USD at the start of July. By Thursday, after margin calls and a forced sale of its leveraged positions at a discount, roughly 35 billion of that was gone.

Many of his AI infrastructure names were up well over 100% this year, even after the July selloff. The fund was up 439% at the end of June.

What killed the fund was not the thesis. It was leverage of nearly 400%, combined with short positions in software that moved against him at the same time as his longs fell. When his top holdings dropped 40-50% in a few weeks, the margin calls came, and he was forced to sell at the worst possible moment.

As you know, I share his conviction. I believe AI is changing our world completely, and my portfolio reflects that, with positions in names like $MU, $LRCX, and $TSM. Several of these were hit hard in July too.

The difference is what happens on the worst days.

Before I size a position, I calculate 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗵𝗮𝗽𝗽𝗲𝗻𝘀 𝘁𝗼 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗳𝗼𝗹𝗶𝗼 𝗶𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗺𝗮𝗿𝗸𝗲𝘁 𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗻𝘀 𝗮𝗴𝗮𝗶𝗻𝘀𝘁 𝗺𝗲 𝗼𝗻 𝗶𝘁𝘀 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝘀𝘁 𝗱𝗮𝘆𝘀. If AI infrastructure drops 40% in a month, like it just did for some names, can I hold through it, or am I forced to sell?

That calculation changes everything about how you build a portfolio.

This is why I use no leverage on concentrated bets. Leverage converts a drawdown into a margin call, and a margin call converts a paper loss into a permanent one. Aschenbrenner never got the chance to be right in the long run, because the market took him out in the short run.

This is also why part of my portfolio sits in health care and other defensive positions with low correlation to the AI trade. When tech is flying, they feel like a drag on returns. 𝗢𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝘀𝘁 𝗱𝗮𝘆𝘀, 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘆 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘀𝗼𝗻 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴, and they buy you the one thing every investor with conviction needs: time to be proven right.

And the worst days will come.

July was a rough month for the AI trade, and my portfolio finished with a drawdown of 5,9%. Not fun, but manageable, and exactly within what my worst-days calculations prepare me for. That is the entire difference between a bad month and losing almost everything.

It is decided long before the bad month arrives.

Conviction tells you what to own. Risk management decides whether you survive long enough to be proven right.

Thanks for copying and following 🙏
